verdict.rationale: Logseq's docs say sync is opt-in per graph, so graphs can stay local-only, and the product presents itself as privacy-first and open source. Community users confirm local data with no mandatory subscription, and some keep graphs in their own git repos. That covers the story's local-only path without the vendor cloud. Missing for 10: a first-party self-hosted sync backend (multi-device sync outside Logseq Sync relies on user workarounds like Syncthing, git or iCloud), and in-depth docs on running fully offline.
